title: Generating Images and Video · Level 2
slo: Describe how diffusion generates an image from a written prompt.

exercises.question_text: Which is a prompt for image generation?

options.text: A dog carrying a stick in its mouth
options.rationale: This is a natural-language description of desired visual content. It can guide a generated scene.
A bounding box records an object's location. It is not a requested scene description.

options.text: A list of pixel class labels
options.rationale: Pixel class labels describe segmentation results. They do not specify a scene to generate.
options.better_fit: Use them to represent semantic segmentation output.

options.rationale: A category is a label predicted for an image. It is not a natural-language request for an image.
options.better_fit: Use it as an image-classification result.

exercises.question_text: An image or video made from a description is created by ___.

parts.text: An image or video made from a description is created by

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The requested visual content would not be created.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Image synthesis creates requested images or video.

exercises.explanation: Image synthesis generates visual content from a description.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The definition does not read correctly.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Define the prompt before stating what it guides.

exercises.correct_answer: A prompt is a natural-language description that guides desired visual features.
exercises.explanation: A prompt is a natural-language description that guides visual features.

exercises.question_text: A designer has only the words “purple mountain at sunrise” and must create a new poster image. Which capability should the designer choose?

options.rationale: The designer needs a new image from words. Image generation creates visual content from a description.
Object detection finds objects in an existing image. It cannot create the requested mountain poster.
options.better_fit: Use it to locate objects in an existing picture.

feedback.intrinsic: The poster would not be created.
feedback.instructional: Use image generation when words must become a new image.

options.rationale: Contextual image analysis interprets supplied visual input. Here there is no image to interpret.
options.better_fit: Use it to describe an existing image.

feedback.intrinsic: The written request would remain unmade.
feedback.instructional: Image generation produces new visual content from language.

options.rationale: Semantic segmentation labels pixels in an existing image. It does not create a poster from a description.
options.better_fit: Use it to identify pixel-level regions in an image.

feedback.intrinsic: The designer would receive pixel labels, not a poster.
feedback.instructional: Generating a new poster from words requires image generation.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The generation process is out of sequence.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Start from noise, build structure, evaluate it, then produce the final image.

exercises.correct_answer: Start with random pixels Remove noise Create structure Evaluate against prompt Produce final image
exercises.explanation: Noise removal creates structure before the developing image is evaluated and finalized.

exercises.question_text: A sign maker needs to enter requests for newly generated produce images. Which entries are suitable prompts? Select all that apply.

options.text: Three red apples in a wooden bowl
options.rationale: This phrase describes desired visual content. It can guide image generation.

options.text: A yellow pear on a white plate
options.rationale: This is a natural-language scene description. It specifies visual features for generation.

options.text: The coordinates of one bounding box
options.rationale: Bounding-box coordinates describe a detected location. They do not describe a requested scene.
options.better_fit: Use them to report an object's location in an existing image.

feedback.intrinsic: The sign request would lack a scene description.
feedback.instructional: Prompts use natural language to describe what should be generated.

options.rationale: A category and confidence score are classification output. They do not request visual content.
options.better_fit: Use this format to report a classification prediction.

feedback.intrinsic: The generator would not receive enough scene detail.
feedback.instructional: A suitable prompt describes the desired subject and visual context.

exercises.question_text: Diffusion begins with ___ before it develops a prompt-matching image.

parts.text: before it develops a prompt-matching image.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The starting state would be misidentified.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Diffusion begins with noise rather than analysis outputs or filter kernels.

exercises.explanation: Diffusion starts from random pixel noise, then iteratively develops structure.

exercises.question_text: The stages that progressively turn noise into the dog-and-stick scene are diffusion ___.

parts.text: The stages that progressively turn noise into the dog-and-stick scene are diffusion

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The process stages would be misidentified.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Diffusion iterations are the repeated stages that progressively form the requested scene.

exercises.explanation: The dog-and-stick scene develops through a sequence of diffusion iterations.

exercises.question_text: A marketing lead needs a method that starts with random pixel values and creates a new produce image matching a written request. Which method should the lead choose?

options.rationale: Diffusion starts with random pixel values and iteratively removes noise. It creates an image matching the prompt.
Semantic segmentation classifies pixels in an existing image. It does not create a new image from noise.
options.better_fit: Use it to identify pixel-level object regions.

feedback.intrinsic: The lead would receive pixel classes, not a new produce image.
feedback.instructional: Diffusion is the generative method described.

options.rationale: Image classification predicts an image label. It does not synthesize a new prompt-matching scene.
options.better_fit: Use it to name the main subject of an existing image.

feedback.intrinsic: The requested image would not be produced.
feedback.instructional: Diffusion generates an image; classification predicts a label.

options.rationale: Object detection reports objects and their locations in an image. It does not generate a new image from random pixels.
options.better_fit: Use it to locate produce in an existing photograph.

feedback.intrinsic: The lead would receive locations instead of a generated image.
feedback.instructional: Choose diffusion when the task is to synthesize a prompt-matching image.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The definition does not read correctly.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Connect events unfolding with their logical sequence over time.

exercises.correct_answer: Temporal progression means events unfold in a logical sequence over time.
exercises.explanation: Temporal progression means events unfold in a logical sequence over time.

exercises.question_text: A fruit-sign image is still mostly random noise after an early generation step. What should the illustrator expect subsequent diffusion iterations to do? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Subsequent iterations remove more noise. This moves the result away from random pixels.
Noise removal makes structure emerge. The requested fruit scene becomes clearer.

options.text: Replace the prompt with a class label.
options.rationale: The prompt remains the generation guide. A class label is not a replacement for it.
options.better_fit: Use class labels in supervised classification training.

feedback.intrinsic: The request would lose its scene guidance.
feedback.instructional: Diffusion continues to evaluate progress against the prompt.

options.text: Stop after the first noisy result.
options.rationale: An early noisy image is not the intended final result. Diffusion uses subsequent iterations to refine it.
options.better_fit: Stopping would be appropriate only after a completed result meets the request.

feedback.intrinsic: The delivered image would remain largely unformed.
feedback.instructional: Continue iterations so noise decreases and scene structure emerges.

exercises.question_text: A producer is reviewing a generated clip of a dog walking with a stick. Which checks should the producer make before delivery? Select all that apply.

options.text: The dog's feet stay on the ground.
options.rationale: Physical behavior must remain plausible in generated video. A walking dog's feet should contact the ground.

options.text: The walking unfolds logically over time.
options.rationale: Temporal progression requires a logical sequence of events. Walking should progress coherently across time.

options.text: Every frame has a class label.
options.rationale: Class labels identify image subjects. They do not ensure physical or temporal coherence in video.
options.better_fit: Use class labels when categorizing still images or frames.

feedback.intrinsic: The clip could still have impossible motion or event order.
feedback.instructional: Review physical behavior and temporal progression for coherent video.

options.text: The clip contains one high-resolution still frame.
options.rationale: A single sharp frame does not establish coherent movement. The producer must review change across time.
options.better_fit: Use this criterion when assessing a still image.

feedback.intrinsic: The clip could still contain inconsistent motion.
feedback.instructional: Video quality also depends on plausible physical behavior and logical temporal progression.
